3106:
** μᾰκᾰρ-ίζω**,
_Attic dialect_ _future_ -ιῶ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 429}}:— **bless, deem** or **pronounce happy, congratulate**, τινα {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.538, 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.11, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.45, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1196 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.4.4, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 911 (Lyric poetry), etc.}}; τινά τινος **for** a thing, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 429, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 2.81, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.194 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus; τινὰ ἐπί τινι [prev. author] “D.” 1.15}}; also μ. τὴν ῥώμην τινός, ={μ. τινὰ τῆς ῥώμης}, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.31}}; ironically, μακαρίσαντες ὑμῶν τὸ ἀπειρόκακον **blessing** your **happy** ignorance, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.105: with _neuter_ _pronoun_, τουτὶ.. σε μόνον (conjecture).. μακαρίζω 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 588}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.51, 3rd c.AD(?): Diogenes Laertius 6.45: with _dative_ modi, σωφροσύνῃ καὶ ὁσιότητι μακαρισθείς 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Cynegeticus” 1.11.}}

3137:
**Μαρία**, -ας (Hellenized form), and Μαριάμ, indecl., ἡ (Aram. מַרְיָם; _Heb._ (MT) מִרְיָם)
Mary. In NT;
1. **the mother of Jesus**: Mat.1:16 ff. Mat.2:11 13:55, Mrk.6:3, Luk.1:27 ff. Luk.2:5, 16 2:19, 34, Act.1:14
2. M. Magdalene (which see).
3. The wife of Clopas (Jhn.19:25) and mother of James the little, **and Joses**: Mat.27:56, 61 28:1, Mrk.15:40, 47 16:1, Luk.24:10.
4. **The sister of Martha and Lazarus**: Luk.10:39, 42 Jhn.11:1-2, 19 ff. Jhn.12:3.
5. **The mother of John Mark**: Act.12:12.
6. A Christian greeted by St. Paul: Rom.16:6 (on the signification of the name, see Zorell, see word; on the use of the alternative forms in NT, _DB_, iii, 278 bn).†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)

** μαστῑγ-όω**,
_optative_ μαστιγοίην (variant -οῖμι) {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.157}}: _future_ -ώσω {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.13}}: _aorist_ -ωσα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.54}}:—_passive_, _future_ μαστιγωθήσομαι {{LXX+5th c.BC+|LXX.Psa.72(73).5, μαστιγώσομαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 361e, “IG” 22.1362.9}}: _aorist_ _participle_ -ωθείς {{Refs 5th c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.180 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus}}:—**whip, flog**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.114 (μαστιγέων codices), 3.16, 7.54; μυρίκῃ ἢ μαλάχῃ 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Ind.” 3}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.18, etc.}}; πληγὰς μαστιγούσθω **let him be whipped**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 914b, compare 845a; ψυχῆς ἠσκημένης καὶ μεμαστιγωμένης 2nd c.AD: Maximus Tyrius Sophista 25.5.}}

3181:
** μεθόριος**, α, ον
(also ος, ον {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus (see. below))}}, (ὅρος) **lying between as a boundary**, γῆ μεθορία τῆς Ἀργείας καὶ Λακωνικῆς the **border** country **between**.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.27, 4.56}}: _neuter_ _plural_, **borders, marches**, ἐν -ίοις τῆς Ἀττικῆς καὶ Βοιωτίας {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.18, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.16, etc.}}; τὰ μ. Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος variant in {{NT+5th c.BC+|NT.Mark.7.24; μεθόρια φιλοσόφου τε καὶ πολιτικοῦ 5th c.BC: Prodicus Philosophus 6: _sing._, τὸ μεθόριον LXX.Josh.19.27 codex A: _metaphorically_, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 878b; ὁ ὕπνος δοκεῖ εἶναι τοῦ ζῆν καὶ τοῦ μὴ ζῆν μ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 778b30, compare “HA” 588b5, 5th c.AD: Hierocles Platonicus Philosophus “in Carmen Aureum - FPG” 20p.462M.}}; ἐν μεθορίῳ [εἶναι] {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 943 b26, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.255}}; ἡ Ἀράβων καὶ Ἀσσυρίων μεθορία (i.e. χώρα) {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Crassus” 22; ἡ μεθόριος 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.514}}; ἔστι ἐν λιτότητι μεθόριος there is a **limit** to frugality, conjecture in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Epicurus Philosophus “Gnomologium Vaticanum - Kleine Schriften” 63.}}
